title: Customers Who Ordered Every Month of 2026
description:
Find customers who placed **at least one order in every month of 2026** (January through March, based on the data provided — 3 months). Return their customer_id and name.

**Table: orders** — `id`, `customer_id`, `order_date`, `status`, `total_amount`

**Table: customers** — `id`, `name`, `email`, `city`, `country`

Output columns: `name`. Order by `name`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR, city VARCHAR, country VARCHAR); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Alice','alice@example.com','New York','USA'),(2,'Bob','bob@example.com','London','UK'),(3,'Carol','carol@example.com','Chicago','USA'); CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer_id INT, order_date DATE, status VARCHAR, total_amount DECIMAL); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1,DATE '2026-01-05','completed',100.00),(2,1,DATE '2026-02-10','completed',200.00),(3,1,DATE '2026-03-15','completed',150.00),(4,2,DATE '2026-01-20','completed',300.00),(5,2,DATE '2026-02-25','completed',250.00),(6,3,DATE '2026-01-30','completed',80.00),(7,3,DATE '2026-03-10','completed',120.00);
solution_sql: SELECT c.name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_date) = 2026 GROUP BY o.customer_id, c.name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date)) = 3 ORDER BY c.name

test_cases.description: Only Alice ordered in all 3 months; Bob missed March; Carol missed February

hints: COUNT(DISTINCT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date)) counts unique months per customer.
HAVING ... = 3 keeps customers who have orders in exactly 3 distinct months.
explanation: Alice has orders in Jan, Feb, Mar (3 distinct months) ✓. Bob has Jan, Feb (2) ✗. Carol has Jan, Mar (2) ✗. HAVING filters to only those with all 3 months covered.
